title: Sample collection procedure - how defence lawyers find loopholes
p1:
A single mistake during sample collection can change the direction of an entire criminal case.

Many people think evidence is only about what was found. But defence lawyers often look at something else: how that evidence was collected.
p2: The surprising part? Even genuine evidence can be questioned if the procedure was not followed properly. A missing signature, unclear record, wrong handling method, or gap in the chain of custody can create doubts about whether the sample remained reliable.
p3:
Sample collection is not just taking a piece of evidence and sending it to a lab. Every step matters — who collected it, when it was collected, how it was stored, and who handled it afterward. Defence lawyers study these details to find weaknesses, not necessarily to prove the evidence is false, but to challenge its trustworthiness.

The lesson: in legal cases, procedure can be as important as proof.
conclusion: Have you ever considered that a small procedural mistake could affect the outcome of a major criminal case?
